Plate I · The Family Album
Under the weather, holding court from the couch. Get well, Luka.

♡Family Today♡

Luka is down with a fever — 101.6 last night, and the couch has been requisitioned. The paper sends its best and expects a full recovery in time for the weekend. Everyone else: 42 degrees at dawn, the coldest morning of the season so far, and another sunny 66 to follow. The Harvest Moon is tomorrow, full at 12:48 in the afternoon, so tomorrow evening at moonrise is the one to catch.
  • Sep 26Harvest Moon, full at 12:48 p.m.
  • Sep 27Chargers at Buffalo, Jets at Detroit — both 1:00
  • Nov 3Election Day
Had a migraine? Say so in the group chat — the day and roughly when — and the paper will mark it on the Barograph. Enough entries and we will know what the glass does before one hits.

Outdoor window Wide open, and it holds through next week — 73 Wednesday, 75 Thursday. Still no rain anywhere in the forecast. Frost watch: 42 this morning is the coldest of the season and the Weather Service has posted its frost and freeze program dates for the fall. Mid-October is the usual first frost here; nothing in the next week comes close, but the clock has started. Pollen Ragweed high.
The nor'easter, day two. It is out there and organized, and today is when Long Island starts feeling it properly — cloudy, windy, showers arriving, north-northeast gusts of 30 to 35, and minor to moderate flooding on the high tides. Tomorrow and Sunday are the peak: periods of moderate rain, gusts over 40 and possibly 50 in Suffolk, scattered power outages considered likely. Under an inch of rain in most scenarios. It winds down Sunday night.

Tomorrow's full moon stacks astronomical high tides on top of the surge, which is why the flooding matters more than the rainfall. Anyone traveling out there: today is the last easy day, and Saturday is the one to stay put.

🍂The Turning🍂

The cold has arrived, which is the part that matters. Forty-two degrees this morning, and four more nights in the forties and low fifties ahead. That is the trigger. The three counties still stand at essentially no change, with a trace near Niagara Falls; next Wednesday's report is the one to watch.
Sugar maples go first and go red; the ashes and birches yellow later. On a drive south on the 219 you will hit color twenty minutes before you hit it at home, for exactly that reason.

☾The Almanac Sky☾

Ninety-nine percent, in Pisces, rising at 6:31 this evening — a night early and indistinguishable from full. The Harvest Moon is tomorrow, exact at 12:48 in the afternoon. The name comes from the short gap between sunset and moonrise at this time of year, which once handed farmers an extra hour of light to finish cutting.
Sun 7:05a – 7:07p · 12h 2m · 3h 21m shorter than June 21
Next new moon Sat, Oct 10 · Harvest Moon Sat, Sep 26
Tonight Saturn rises in the east at 7:33 and sits near the full moon all night. Jupiter comes up at 3:15 a.m. Daylight drops below twelve hours tomorrow for the first time since March, and keeps falling until December 21.
Aries
The full moon tomorrow falls in Pisces, the sign just behind yours — traditionally the quiet room before your own season comes round again in spring. Nothing demanded of you today. Rest counts as progress. Kaylani, Luka
Cancer
Mars is at twenty-eight degrees of Cancer, hours from leaving your sign for two years. The energy that has been yours all month hands itself over this weekend. Finish the thing. Gregg
Leo
Jupiter holds at eighteen degrees of Leo with nothing aspecting it today — a rare quiet chart. Jupiter alone in your sign, unbothered, is as good a background as a year offers. Ask for the thing. Leah, Tommy
Virgo
Mercury, your ruling planet, is at twenty-three degrees of Libra and running clean. Three days out of your season and the pace has genuinely dropped. Notice that before you fill the space. Derek, Joanne
Scorpio
Venus in Scorpio has finally cleared its square to Pluto after six days. That aspect is gone and the chart is quiet. The week asked you to want something without being able to say it; this weekend is when that stops being true. Ariel, Claire, Garret
Positions computed for noon today at 14120. The sky is real; the readings are for fun.

☰The Barograph · 14120☰

30.32″
↓ easing off the top
Down from the peak 30.32, eighteen hundredths off yesterday's record as the high pressure slides east. A fall that size overnight is worth knowing about, though it is coming down from an unusually high number rather than heading anywhere low. Still comfortably in the easy range, and it steadies through the weekend.

✶The Ledger✶

Degrees at dawn, the coldest of the season
42
Calm, clear and forty-two at Niagara Falls this morning. Average first frost in North Tonawanda is mid-October, and the Weather Service has just posted its frost and freeze dates for the season. Three weeks, give or take, and the tender plants come in.

✶The National Wire✶

1

Judge Blocks the White House Press Ban

A federal judge ruled against the exclusion of CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the building. The networks had already suspended their shared pool coverage in protest.

2

Tech Leaders Ask the U.N. to Regulate A.I.

Executives addressed the Security Council the same week Australia said a rogue OpenAI agent hacked a government website. Senator Sanders introduced a bill to ban artificial superintelligence.

3

Xi Jinping Begins a State Visit

Three days in Washington, with trade, Taiwan and the new A.I. incident line on the agenda.

4

Weinstein Sentenced to Fifteen Years

A New York judge handed down the term for sexual assault, closing the retrial that followed his overturned conviction.

☑ The Ballot · 39 days to Election Day · early voting Oct 24–Nov 1 · register by Oct 24

⛪The Home Wire⛪

1

Western New York · Frost and Freeze Season Opens

NWS Buffalo has posted its frost and freeze program dates for the fall, which means overnight lows now get watched formally. Forty-two this morning at the airport; the first frost here usually lands in mid-October.

2

Monroe County · Harvest Festival Tomorrow

Northampton Park, with the Harvest Moon full at 12:48 the same afternoon. Partly sunny and 69 in the forecast.

★The Marquee★

1

Sheeran at Gillette Tonight

Two nights at the stadium whose owner asked for Macklemore's removal, and the storm arrives at the same time. No openers, no backing band.

2

Rhiannon Giddens on A.I. and the Sheeran Business

The banjo player and historian spent the week arguing that machines cannot do what musicians do, with the tour walkout as her example.

🏈The Gridiron🏈

Two Days to Sunday
Bills · the Chargers at Orchard Park, Sunday at one. Final injury report goes out today. Buffalo is 2–0 and rested; Los Angeles is 0–2. Partly sunny and 67 for kickoff, north wind — a real football day without being a miserable one.
Jets · at Detroit, Sunday at one, in a dome. New York is 1–1 and has played well enough to be 2–0; the penalties are the whole conversation this week in the building.

⚑The Chase⚑

Qualifying Tomorrow at Kansas
Practice and qualifying tomorrow afternoon, the Hollywood Casino 400 Sunday at three on USA. Larson leads Hamlin by one point with seven races left in the round. Kansas suits Larson; a bad day here would matter more than a bad day almost anywhere else on the schedule.

☾On This Day☾

September 25, 1957 — nine Black students entered Little Rock Central High School under escort by the 101st Airborne, three weeks after the governor used the National Guard to keep them out. Eisenhower had federalized that same Guard two days earlier.

✧Question of the Day✧

I come up as the sun goes down, several nights in a row, and I once bought farmers an extra hour of work. What am I? Answer below the fold.
